election.name: Illinois General Primary Election
election.earlyVoting: Lincoln Park Branch Library, 1150 W. Fullerton Ave.
election.note: Illinois is a semi-open primary: you declare a party at the polls and receive that party's ballot. Choosing Independent gives you only referenda. All judicial and most county seats were won by Democrats in recent cycles — the Democratic primary is effectively the deciding election for those offices.

races.title: U.S. Senate — Illinois
races.description: Dick Durbin is retiring after 5 terms — the first open Illinois Senate seat since 2010. This is effectively decided by the Democratic primary in a statewide D+9 state.

candidates.name: Raja Krishnamoorthi
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative for IL-8 (northwest suburbs) since 2017. Born in New Delhi, moved to U.S. as a child. Princeton mechanical engineering/public policy; Harvard Law J.D. Policy director for Obama's 2004 Senate campaign. Raised ~$30M; received ~$10M from Fairshake PAC (crypto-aligned).
endorsements: Former Obama chief of staff Bill Daley

candidates.name: Juliana Stratton
candidates.bio: Incumbent Lt. Governor of Illinois (2019–2026). First Black woman elected Lt. Governor of Illinois. Former state representative. First to announce after Durbin's retirement. Pritzker funneled $14M into Illinois Future PAC supporting her. Late-breaking polls showed her potentially overtaking Krishnamoorthi.
priorities: Middle-class tax cuts funded by millionaire tax
endorsements: Governor JB Pritzker (via Illinois Future PAC)

candidates.name: Robin Kelly
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative for IL-2 (south suburbs) since 2013. Previously IL state representative and chief of staff to State Treasurer Alexi Giannoulias. Advocates the most aggressive immigration stance in the field (dismantle ICE and DHS entirely).

candidates.name: Steve Botsford Jr.
candidates.bio: Business owner; ran for Chicago City Council in 2023. Notre Dame graduate. Worked on Capitol Hill for Rep. Tony Cárdenas. M.A. in applied economics (Georgetown), MBA (Northwestern).

candidates.name: Awisi A. Bustos
candidates.bio: Nonprofit executive; former CEO of Illinois Alliance of Boys & Girls Clubs ($11M budget). First-generation Ghanaian American. Daughter-in-law of former U.S. Rep. Cheri Bustos.
priorities: Preparing communities for AI and technology

candidates.name: Jonathan Dean
candidates.bio: Activist, entrepreneur, litigator; describes himself as a proud survivor of childhood sexual abuse. Focused on youth, working families, and civil liberties.

candidates.name: Bryan Maxwell
candidates.bio: PhD in agricultural engineering; research focused on sustainability and environmental issues. Platform includes opposition to U.S. military aid to Israel.

candidates.name: Sean Brown
candidates.bio: Attorney.

candidates.name: Kevin Ryan
candidates.bio: Retired U.S. Marine and teacher.

candidates.name: Christopher Swann
candidates.bio: Nonprofit leader.

candidates.name: Don Tracy
candidates.bio: Attorney; former Illinois Republican Party Chairman (2021–2024); former IL Gaming Board member (2015–2019). Raised ~$2.1M.
priorities: Lower cost-of-living via new energy policies and deregulation

candidates.name: Jeannie Evans
candidates.bio: Attorney specializing in antitrust enforcement. Motivated by shooting death of her brother.

candidates.name: R. Cary Capparelli
candidates.bio: Professor of online geography/geosciences at South Dakota State University; global management/marketing executive. Son of late Democratic state rep Ralph C. Capparelli. Organized first U.S.–Soviet motorsports competitions.

candidates.name: Casey Chlebek
candidates.bio: Emigrated from Poland to U.S. in the 1960s; IT professional at Northern Trust Bank. Previously ran in 2020 and 2022 IL Senate races.

candidates.name: Pamela Denise Long
candidates.bio: Occupational therapist and political commentator.
priorities: Eliminate federal income tax / replace with consumption tax

candidates.name: Jimmy Lee Tillman II
candidates.bio: Author, historian, founder of Martin Luther King Republicans (Black Republicans in Illinois); Heritage Foundation Academy Fellow.
priorities: Ban transgender women from women's sports

races.title: U.S. House — Illinois 5th Congressional District
races.description: Covers Chicago's North Side (including Ward 43) and northwest suburbs. Cook PVI: D+19. The Democratic primary winner is the prohibitive favorite in November.

candidates.name: Mike Quigley
candidates.bio: 17-year incumbent. Previously Cook County Commissioner. Known for work on House Intelligence Committee, government transparency, and LGBTQ+ issues. Re-elected 2024 with 69%. Has soft-launched a potential 2027 Chicago mayoral run if re-elected.

candidates.name: Matt Conroy
candidates.bio: Age 37. Father killed in the September 11 attacks; raised in a single-parent household. Economics degree from Northeastern. Career spanning finance, real estate, technology, and manufacturing.

candidates.name: Ellen A. Corley
candidates.bio: Age 70. Former high school teacher and marketing research consultant. Has run in several Chicago elections as a write-in candidate.

candidates.name: Anthony Michael Tamez
candidates.bio: Age 26. Native American. Elected member of the Chicago Police 17th District Council. Born and raised in IL-5.

candidates.name: Tom Hanson
candidates.bio: Business owner. Has challenged Quigley in every congressional election since 2018.

candidates.name: Dr. Kimball Ladien
candidates.bio: Psychiatrist, age 74. Former 47th Ward aldermanic candidate; ran in 2020 Republican primary for this seat. Advocates his 'Chicago Project' to combat crime and establish world-class schools.
priorities: Unifying Republicans and Democrats around results

candidates.name: Barry Wicker
candidates.bio: North Center resident; first-time candidate. 10 years as a government-licensed financial broker; 10 years as a licensed union engineer.

races.title: Governor / Lieutenant Governor
races.description: Governor and Lt. Governor run as a joint ticket in both the primary and general election. A third Pritzker term would be the first by a Democratic governor in Illinois history.

candidates.name: J.B. Pritzker / Christian Mitchell
candidates.bio: Pritzker has served since 2019; heir to Hyatt hotel fortune; won in 2018 and 2022. Mitchell was IL state representative (2013–2019) then deputy governor (2019–2023); led efforts to ban assault weapons, advance clean energy, and create infrastructure jobs. Pritzker is rumored to be eyeing a 2028 presidential run.

candidates.name: Darren Bailey / Aaron Del Mar
candidates.bio: Bailey is a downstate farmer and former state senator; 2022 Republican gubernatorial nominee (lost to Pritzker by ~13 points). Once called for Chicago to leave the state; fought COVID-19 restrictions. Del Mar is Cook County Republican Party chair, added to court moderate suburban voters.

candidates.name: Ted Dabrowski / Carrie Mendoza
candidates.bio: Dabrowski is former president of Wirepoints (conservative fiscal commentary); former VP of Policy at Illinois Policy Institute. Wilmette resident; has never held elected office. Mendoza is an emergency physician. Dabrowski leads Bailey in recent fundraising.

candidates.name: Rick Heidner / Christina Neitzke-Troike
candidates.bio: Heidner is a video gambling mogul (Gold Rush Gaming) and real estate entrepreneur (Ricky Rocket's Fuel Centers, Prairie State Energy, Heidner Properties). Has donated to both parties over 30 years. Contributed $1M+ to his own campaign. Neitzke-Troike is Mayor of Homer Glen, IL.

candidates.name: James Mendrick / Robert Renteria
candidates.bio: Mendrick is DuPage County Sheriff since 2018 (second term); 30+ year DuPage County resident; financial crimes investigator background. Refused to enforce Illinois' 2023 assault weapon ban. Renteria is an author, Army veteran, and activist.
priorities: Coordinate with ICE to remove criminal migrants from jails

races.title: Attorney General
races.description: The AG is the state's chief law enforcement officer and represents Illinois in legal proceedings.

candidates.name: Kwame Raoul
candidates.bio: AG since 2019; seeking third term. Former IL state senator — succeeded Barack Obama in that seat. Record includes: Organized Retail Crime Task Force, sued gun manufacturers, Crime Gun Connect database, 'Know Your Rights' guide on abortion access after Dobbs, increased Violent Crimes Assistance Program funding.

candidates.name: Bob Fioretti
candidates.bio: Civil rights attorney; former Democratic Chicago alderman (2007–2015, 2nd Ward) who switched to Republican Party. Was 2024 Republican nominee for Cook County State's Attorney; 2022 Republican nominee for Cook County Board President; ran as Independent for Chicago mayor in 2019.

candidates.name: Andy Williams Jr.
candidates.bio: Minister from Darien, IL; ran for president in 2020.

races.title: Secretary of State
races.description: The Secretary of State manages driver's licenses, vehicle registrations, business filings, the state library system, and the state archives. The SOS office has 4,000+ employees.

candidates.name: Alexi Giannoulias
candidates.bio: First elected SOS in 2022; previously elected IL State Treasurer at age 30 in 2006 (youngest state treasurer in the country). Has $6M+ in campaign coffers. Has been floated as a potential 2027 Chicago mayoral candidate.

candidates.name: Diane Harris
candidates.bio: Joliet businesswoman; 30+ years at ComEd, IBEW steward. Joliet Junior College trustee; Joliet Public Library trustee; Republican precinct committeewoman. Ran in 2022 IL Senate race (43rd District, lost by 12 points). Chicago Tribune endorsed Harris over Adamczyk.

candidates.name: Walter Adamczyk
candidates.bio: Republican committeeman for Chicago's 29th Ward (second term); active in election judge recruitment and conservative organizing on Chicago's Northwest/West Side. Ran as write-in aldermanic candidate in 2023. 30 years of bookkeeping/accounting experience.
priorities: Free driver's licenses/IDs for honorably discharged veterans
Dedicated express lanes for veterans at SOS facilities

races.title: Comptroller
races.description: The Comptroller manages state finances, signs off on state payments, and provides financial oversight. Incumbent Susana Mendoza is not seeking re-election.

candidates.name: Margaret Croke
candidates.bio: IL state representative for District 12 (Lincoln Park, Old Town, Gold Coast) since 2020 — the same seat contested in the race below. Backed by Gov. Pritzker, House Speaker Welch, Cook County Democratic Party, numerous legislators, labor unions, and banks. Considered the establishment's top choice.
priorities: Create transparent public portal for all state expenditures

candidates.name: Karina Villa
candidates.bio: Former school social worker; IL state senator (25th District, west suburbs) since 2019. Known for environmental and education legislation. Backed by Senate President Don Harmon and U.S. Rep. Delia Ramirez. Most progressive anti-Trump candidate in the race.
priorities: Raise new revenue (digital advertising tax, graduated income tax)

candidates.name: Stephanie Kifowit
candidates.bio: Longest-tenured candidate in this race; IL state representative since 2013. U.S. Marine Corps veteran; former financial advisor. Backed by multiple labor unions, veterans groups, some House Democrats, and suburban elected officials.

candidates.name: Holly Kim
candidates.bio: Lake County Treasurer and Collector since 2018. First Korean American elected to countywide office in Illinois history. Endorsed by outgoing Comptroller Mendoza. Has earned votes in historically conservative Lake County.

candidates.name: Bryan Drew
candidates.bio: Attorney from Benton, IL (downstate).

races.title: Treasurer
races.description: The Treasurer manages and invests state funds and oversees college savings programs (Bright Start/Bright Directions) and financial literacy initiatives. No Republican filed a valid petition — first time in at least 90 years a major party has failed to field a candidate for a statewide Illinois office.

candidates.name: Mike Frerichs
candidates.bio: IL State Treasurer since 2015; seeking fourth term. Yale BA; formerly managed engineering firm Smart Structures LLC; taught English in Illinois and Taiwan. Previously IL State Senator (District 52, 2007–2015). Has expanded Bright Start college savings and returned record amounts of unclaimed property to residents.

candidates.name: Max Rice
candidates.status: Write-in candidate — needs 5,000 votes to appear in November
candidates.bio: Also running as write-in in Republican U.S. Senate primary. Must receive 5,000 write-in votes to appear on the November general election ballot.

candidates.name: Max Solomon
candidates.status: Write-in candidate — needs 5,000 votes to appear in November
candidates.bio: B.A. in Political Science, M.A. in Theology, J.D. in Law; attorney; adjunct professor; ordained Christian minister. Served as Grande Prairie Public Library trustee. Previously endorsed by Illinois Family Action in 2020 state representative run.

races.title: Illinois State Senate — District 6
races.description: District 6 covers the lakefront neighborhoods of Lake View, Lincoln Park, and Near North Side. Incumbent Feigenholtz faces her first primary challenger in 31 years. The Chicago Tribune editorial board endorsed Uniejewski.

candidates.name: Sara Feigenholtz
candidates.bio: State Senator since 2020; state representative for District 12 from 1994. Age 69. Career focused on healthcare, social services, and LGBTQ+ rights. Backed by labor and establishment Democrats.
candidates.note: The Illinois Democratic Party spent $190,000 on mailers supporting Feigenholtz — more than any other General Assembly candidate since September 2025.

candidates.name: Nick Uniejewski
candidates.bio: Policy analyst, formerly for the City of Chicago. Loyola University Chicago BA (2017); DePaul graduate degree (2019). Would be the second openly gay state senator in Illinois history. Served as campaign manager for former U.S. Rep. Marie Newman.
priorities: Housing supply (legalizing coach houses, zoning reform)

races.title: Illinois State House — District 12
races.description: Covers Gold Coast, Old Town, Lincoln Park, and East Lakeview. Incumbent Margaret Croke is vacating the seat to run for Comptroller (above). Four Democrats compete for an open seat in a D+20 district.

candidates.name: Paul Kendrick
candidates.bio: Former Obama campaign and administration official; nonprofit leadership roles. Endorsed by incumbent Rep. Croke and State Sen. Feigenholtz. One of four IL legislative candidates benefiting from a Meta (Facebook/Instagram parent)-funded PAC.

candidates.name: Karim Lakhani
candidates.bio: Chief development officer for his family's Chicago-area hotel business. Campaign largely self-funded. Endorsed by the Chicago Teachers Union.

candidates.name: Mac LeBuhn
candidates.bio: Former legal counsel and policy advisor to Mayor Lori Lightfoot. Emphasizes ethics reform and experience in city government.

candidates.name: Litcy Kurisinkal
candidates.bio: Biden 2020 campaign alumna. Attended protests against ICE operations at the Broadview detention facility. Running the most grassroots campaign in the field.

candidates.name: Justin Kumar
candidates.bio: Running as the Republican candidate for Illinois House District 12.

races.title: Cook County Board President
races.description: Chief executive of Cook County, overseeing the county jail, court system, public health system (Stroger Hospital), forest preserves, and a $10B+ annual budget with 22,000+ employees. In an overwhelmingly blue county, the Democratic primary winner is virtually certain to win in November.

candidates.name: Toni Preckwinkle
candidates.bio: First Black woman elected Cook County Board President. Before that, 4th Ward alderman for nearly 20 years, then a high school history teacher for 10 years. Chair of Cook County Democratic Party since 2018. Turns 79 on primary day (March 17). A 5th term would tie her with George Dunne as county's longest-serving leader.
candidates.note: Preckwinkle's record: 15 years of balanced budgets without property tax hikes; $600M+ in medical debt forgiven for 500K+ residents; four bond rating upgrades since 2021; guaranteed income for 3,000+ households.

candidates.name: Brendan Reilly
candidates.bio: Chicago 42nd Ward Alderman since 2007 (Loop, River North, Streeterville, Magnificent Mile, West Loop). Age 54. Former IL House staffer; former AT&T executive. Close ally of Mayor Rahm Emanuel; later backed Paul Vallas over Lightfoot; frequent critic of Mayor Brandon Johnson.
candidates.note: Preckwinkle has tied Reilly to Trump through campaign donations Reilly says were donated to charity.

races.title: Cook County Assessor
races.description: Sets the taxable value of all 1.8 million parcels in Cook County, directly determining property tax bills. This race pits a reform incumbent against a challenger endorsed by the Cook County Democratic Party organization.

candidates.name: Fritz Kaegi
candidates.bio: Former financial analyst and mutual fund portfolio manager who ran on a reform platform. Has fought historic disparities that over-assessed lower-value residential properties while under-assessing commercial properties. Has clashed with the Cook County Democratic organization throughout his tenure.
candidates.note: Cook County Democratic Party endorsed his challenger rather than the incumbent — unusual for a sitting officeholder.

candidates.name: Pat Hynes
candidates.bio: Lyons Township Assessor (first term); firefighter/EMT with Western Springs Fire Department. Spent 23 years in the Cook County Assessor's office as a residential field inspector (including three under Kaegi). Nephew of Thomas Hynes (5-term Cook County Assessor, former IL Senate President).
priorities: Using building permit data to improve accuracy
candidates.note: Has taken nearly $70,000 from property tax attorneys at law firms providing property tax services. Real estate industry donors favor Hynes over Kaegi.

candidates.name: Nico Tsatsoulis
candidates.bio: Has worked in finance, retail/wholesale, and real estate. Also ran for assessor in the 2022 general election.

races.title: Cook County Clerk
races.description: Oversees suburban Cook County elections, vital records (births, deaths, marriages), real estate tax records, and official county proceedings. Annual budget: $75M; 350 employees.

candidates.name: Monica Gordon
candidates.bio: Sworn in December 2, 2024; won a special election with 65% after incumbent Karen Yarbrough died in April 2024. Former Cook County Commissioner. Describes Yarbrough as her 'mentor.'

candidates.name: Hontas Farmer
candidates.bio: Running as Libertarian candidate for Cook County Clerk.

races.title: Cook County Sheriff
races.description: Leads the Cook County Jail and the 2nd largest sheriff's department in the U.S. (6,700+ officers and civilians).

candidates.name: Thomas Dart
candidates.bio: Cook County Sheriff since 2006; seeking re-election. Former IL state senator (14th District) and state representative (28th District); in Illinois politics since 1991.

candidates.name: Brad Sandefur
candidates.bio: Deputy Sheriff Sergeant with 36 years in the department (17 as shift commander). Certified police officer, correctional officer, tactical officer, and academy instructor. Trained with FBI, Secret Service, and Federal Bureau of Prisons. U.S. Marine Corps veteran. M.S. in Criminal Justice/Forensic Psychology from Liberty University.
priorities: Alternatives to incarceration for youth and non-violent first offenders
Remove political influence from law enforcement

races.title: Cook County Treasurer
races.description: Manages and invests Cook County's funds, oversees property tax collection and distribution, and publishes annual property tax research.

candidates.name: Maria Pappas
candidates.bio: Cook County Treasurer since 1998; this would be her 7th re-election. Greek American attorney born June 7, 1949. Touts: property tax research team publications; plans to create an AI unit. Has announced a 2027 Chicago mayoral candidacy.

races.title: Cook County Board of Review — District 1
races.description: The Board of Review hears appeals from property owners who believe their assessments are incorrect. District 1 covers much of the western end of Cook County.

candidates.name: George Cardenas
candidates.bio: Current District 1 Board of Review Commissioner; oversees the property tax appeals process for western Cook County.

candidates.name: Juanita Irizarry
candidates.bio: Former executive director of Friends of the Parks. Backed by Assessor Fritz Kaegi. Endorsed by Ald. Daniel La Spata.
priorities: Make corporations pay their fair share in property taxes

races.title: Cook County Board of Review — District 2
races.description: District 2 covers northern Cook County. This is a contested race between an incumbent and a well-connected Democratic operative.

candidates.name: Samantha Steele
candidates.bio: Elected in 2022; represents northern Cook County. Notably does not take money from the property tax appeal industry. Involved in a 2024 controversy involving a fired employee with a prior federal guilty plea.

candidates.name: Elizabeth (Liz) Nicholson
candidates.bio: Longtime Democratic campaign operative; top adviser for three decades to former state Senate President John Cullerton. Backed by members of Congress and numerous elected officials.

races.title: Cook County Board of Commissioners — District 12
races.description: Ward 43 is in Cook County Commission District 12. Incumbent Bridget Degnen is retiring. The original endorsed candidate (Catherine 'Cat' Sharp) dropped out due to a federal court case related to ICE protests at Broadview.

candidates.name: Elizabeth Granato
candidates.bio: Cook County's current Asset Management chief. Has led the fundraising and endorsement count in this race after the original endorsed candidate withdrew.

candidates.name: José 'Che-Che' Wilson
candidates.bio: Community advocate and challenger in the District 12 race.

candidates.name: Isaiah White
candidates.bio: Community challenger in the District 12 race.

races.title: Illinois Appellate Court — 1st District (Hoffman Vacancy)
races.description: 10-year term. Vacancy created by the death of Justice Thomas E. Hoffman in July 2025. No Republicans filed; Democratic primary winner is virtually certain to win in November.

candidates.name: Judith C. Rice
candidates.bio: Cook County Circuit Court judge since 2014; presiding judge over the domestic violence division since 2021. Would be the first openly lesbian woman to serve on the Illinois Appellate Court. Slated by Cook County Democratic Party.

races.title: Cook County Circuit Court — Countywide (Burke Vacancy)
races.description: Vacancy of the Hon. Kathleen Marie Burke. No Republicans filed.

candidates.name: Steven Q. McKenzie
candidates.bio: Assistant corporation counsel supervisor in the City of Chicago's Law Department since 2006.

races.title: Cook County Circuit Court — Countywide (Cobbs Vacancy)
races.description: Vacancy of the Hon. Cynthia Y. Cobbs. Contested race: the slated candidate vs. an appointed judge. No Republicans filed.

candidates.name: Luz Maria Toledo
candidates.status: Slated (endorsed by Cook County Democratic Party)
candidates.bio: Cook County Assistant State's Attorney since 2007 (currently Civil Actions Bureau/Real Estate Litigation). Previously 12+ years in criminal division prosecuting traffic, misdemeanor, and felony cases. Admitted to IL bar 2006.

candidates.name: Linda Sackey
candidates.bio: Appointed judge January 2025; currently in Traffic Division. Previously clerked for IL Supreme Court Justice Mary Jane Theis; Assistant IL Attorney General in Civil Appeals Division (2013–2018). Passed over for slating despite judicial appointment. Admitted to IL bar 2006.
endorsements: Girl, I Guess Progressive Voter Guide

races.title: Cook County Circuit Court — Countywide (Coghlan Vacancy)
races.description: Vacancy of the Hon. Mary Ellen Coghlan. Contested race. Note: Cabonargi has faced scrutiny over ethics questions and campaign finance violations. No Republicans filed.

candidates.name: Michael Cabonargi
candidates.bio: Currently in Traffic Division at Daley Center. Previously Regional Director of U.S. Dept. of Health and Human Services (Great Lakes Region); Cook County Board of Review Commissioner (2011–2022).
candidates.note: Has faced scrutiny over ethical questions and campaign finance violations; rated 'WQ' (lower tier) by the Chicago Council of Lawyers.

candidates.name: Ashonta C. Rice
candidates.bio: Private attorney specializing in family law, real estate, probate, and criminal law. Former assistant public guardian for the Cook County Office of the Public Guardian (2004–2007).

races.title: Cook County Circuit Court — Countywide (Hooks Vacancy)
races.description: Vacancy of the Hon. William Hooks. No Republicans filed.

candidates.name: Ava George Stewart
candidates.bio: Private attorney handling criminal defense and civil litigation. Former chief of the misdemeanor and traffic division for the Lake County State's Attorney's Office (2021–2023).

races.title: Cook County Circuit Court — Countywide (Karkula Vacancy)
races.description: Vacancy of the Hon. Paul Karkula. No Republicans filed.

candidates.name: D'Anthony 'Tony' Thedford
candidates.status: Unopposed in primary; appointed to bench by IL Supreme Court
candidates.bio: Slated by Cook County Democratic Party.
endorsements: CBA: Highly Qualified — the highest bar rating in any countywide judicial race this cycle

races.title: Metropolitan Water Reclamation District — Commissioner (6-Year Term)
races.description: MWRD governs flood protection and water quality for Chicago and 128 surrounding communities. This is a multi-winner race: 3 seats are open and the top 3 vote-getters win. Vote for UP TO 3 candidates.

candidates.name: Precious Brady-Davis
candidates.bio: Appointed by Gov. Pritzker July 2023; elected commissioner in 2024. First Black openly transgender woman appointed and elected to public office in Cook County history; first to serve on a water reclamation district in the U.S.

candidates.name: Eira Lizeth Corral Sepúlveda
candidates.bio: First Latina elected to MWRD Board; also youngest and first Commissioner from the Northwest suburbs of Cook County in recent history.

candidates.name: Beth McElroy Kirkwood
candidates.bio: Former Orland Township committeewoman; former chair of Moraine Valley Community College board of trustees; former educator in Orland Park schools.

candidates.name: Sarah Bury
candidates.bio: Environmental lawyer; first-time candidate. Sierra Club volunteer (organization has endorsed her). Pursued compliance with transparency provisions in stormwater permits.

candidates.name: Frank Rowder
candidates.bio: Running as the Republican candidate for MWRD Commissioner.

races.title: Metropolitan Water Reclamation District — Commissioner (2-Year Unexpired Term)
races.description: Unexpired 2-year term on the MWRD Board of Commissioners.

candidates.name: Cameron Davis
candidates.bio: Born April 1, 1964; resident of Evanston. Clean water advocate for 40+ years. Served as President Obama's 'Great Lakes Czar' — coordinated work of 11 federal departments to invest $2B+ in Great Lakes restoration. Former president and CEO of the Alliance for the Great Lakes. Former environmental professor at University of Michigan Law School.
